Title: Trump instructs Pentagon to reduce military exercises with South Korea
Article:
UNITED STATES: US President Donald Trump has instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, he said on Sunday in a social media post that also mentioned Seoul's refusal to take part in actions against Iran.
Hours before exercises were scheduled to begin, Trump said in a post on his Truth Social site that although it was too late to cancel the exercises entirely, he was "not happy" that the United States had previously agreed to participate.
The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercises are scheduled to run from Aug 17 to 27, with about 18,000 South Korean military personnel participating. The drills are expected to include operations to counter drones, disrupt GPS signals and cyberattacks to adapt to North Korea's evolving capabilities, officials said last week.
In his social media post, the US president also cited his "very good relationship" with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
"These exercises are not only costly... but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, has been unthreatening and respectful," Trump wrote.
He also pointed to South Korea's stance on the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.
"While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, 'No thanks!'" Trump wrote.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for more information on Trump's request to reduce the military drills. The Pentagon also did not immediately respond.
Pyongyang routinely denounces the US-South Korean exercises as preparations for an invasion.
North Korea last Wednesday fired a ballistic missile from its eastern coast towards the Sea of Japan, the South Korean and Japanese militaries said, six days after a similar North Korean short-range ballistic missile launch on Aug 6.
US military officials have said that North Korean troops, who have fought alongside Russia in its invasion of Ukraine, have gained experience from the conflict, including the growing use of unmanned systems, electronic warfare and cyber operations.
Ukraine said last week that North Korean-made missiles were used in a Russian ballistic missile attack on a steel plant in Zaporizhzhia that killed seven workers and forced a production halt, with Russia's Zircon hypersonic missiles also used in the attack.

Title: Rate shock, ringgit swings drive Tabung Haji's RM278mil London loss [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Tabung Haji said its London property unit's RM278.4 million loss in 2023 was largely due to higher interest rates in the United Kingdom, weaker property valuations and currency movements.
The loss at its investment vehicle LTH Property Holdings 3 Ltd (LTHP3), which bought Great Minster House for RM1.32 billion (£247.5 million)
in 2022, comprised RM303 million in valuation losses and RM275 million in currency losses.
This was partly offset by an operating profit of RM28.2 million.
But Tabung Haji did not disclose the property's current valuation when responding to questions from
Business Times
.
£180 MILLION TO £202 MILLION ESTIMATE
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia associate professor in property economics Dr Muhammad Najib Razali estimated that Great Minster House's value could have fallen to between £180 million and £202 million, based on estimated rental income and prevailing market yields.
That implies a capital decline of roughly 18 to 27 per cent from the acquisition price, although the estimate does not capture rental income or other components of the investment's total return.
Najib said the estimated market value should not be interpreted as Tabung Haji's overall loss on the investment.
Great Minster House continues to generate rental income, he added, and the investments total return also depends on financing costs, currency movements, taxes and transaction costs.
Tabung Haji said LTHP3's
valuation losses were mainly caused by higher interest rates and prevailing market conditions, while adverse foreign exchange movements accounted for the currency losses.
The operating profit reflected income generated by the asset after operating costs.
The  fund said Great Minster House has remained operationally profitable since its acquisition.
LTHP3 acquired Great Minster House from Singapore-listed Sinarmas Land Ltd.
The freehold property was reportedly acquired at a price broadly in line with independent valuations of about £250 million at the time.
The central London office building is occupied by the UK Department for Transport under a long-term lease, with contractual rental increases.
It was also reported that the property generated annual rental income of about £7.18 million when acquired, translating into an initial yield of about 2.9 per cent.
Tabung Haji said the property remains substantially occupied and benefits from its long-term tenancy with the department.
"Its operating returns remain broadly comparable with prevailing market performance."
The sharp increase in UK interest rates, particularly in 2023, put pressure on the property's valuation.
Higher interest rates generally push up the yields required by investors, which in turn puts downward pressure on commercial property prices.
The Bank of England raised its benchmark rate to 5.25 per cent in August 2023, its highest level in more than 15 years.
Rates have since fallen to 3.75 per cent and  have remained there since last December.
LTHP3's loss narrowed sharply to about RM6.4 million in 2024, from RM278.4 million in 2023.
Tabung Haji said the lower-rate environment could provide a more supportive backdrop for property valuations over the medium term.
It said its focus was on improving the asset's income, occupancy and long-term value rather than short-term valuation movements.
RETURN TARGET UNDER SCRUTINY
Tabung Haji did not disclose a specific rental yield target for Great Minster House in its response.
It said only that the property's operating returns remains broadly comparable with prevailing market performance.
Najib said  the reported 2.9 per cent initial yield was below Tabung Haji's previously stated expectation of generating about five per cent annually from the investment.
He said the acquisition price was broadly defensible based on London office market conditions at the time.
But the relatively low initial yield suggested the investment was priced aggressively from a return perspective, Najib added.
"A property can be fairly valued in the market and still be less attractive from a portfolio perspective if the expected return does not adequately compensate for interest-rate, liquidity, currency and concentration risks."
The subsequent rise in UK interest rates and commercial property yields put further pressure on office valuations, contributing to LTHP3's RM278.4 million loss in 2023.
Najib said such valuation movements were a normal feature of commercial property investment.
"If market yields rise from around 2.9 per cent to above four per cent, the increase in the required rate of return can reduce capital value substantially."
Based on assumed annual rental income of £8.1 million this year, Najib estimated that a four per cent market yield implies a value of about £202 million.
At a 4.25 per cent yield, the implied value would be about £190 million, while a 4.5 per cent yield would put the value at around £180 million.
GOVERNMENT TENANT CUSHIONS RISK
Juwai IQI co-founder and group chief executive officer Kashif Ansari said Great Minster House retained characteristics that institutional investors typically look for, including a long lease, government occupation and contractual rental increases.
"Assets like this have held their value well," he said, citing the 2025 acquisition of nearby Francis House by a pension scheme at a net initial yield of around five per cent.
"On that basis, an asset like Great Minster House would likely be valued broadly in the region of what Tabung Haji paid in 2022. You would need a proper valuation to be precise."
Still, publicly available information does not provide a complete standalone picture of Great Minster House's cumulative rental income, financing costs, current market value, debt position or expected exit value.
Najib said the investment, therefore, needed to be assessed on its total risk-adjusted return rather than property value movements alone.
"This is also why empirical analysis is important in institutional property investment. Before committing around RM1.3 billion to one asset, the investment committee should test different assumptions for interest rates, rental growth, market yields, currency movements and exit values."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bus accident kills at least eight in Brazil
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: A bus overturned in a steep, mountainous region north of Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, killing at least eight people, firefighters said in a statement.
Local media reported another two victims had died after being transported from the scene, and said the dead included nine women and a young girl.
The Rio de Janeiro fire department said the accident had taken place early on Sunday near Petropolis, a mountain city north of Rio de Janeiro.
"Firefighters had to perform excavation work to access and extricate some of the passengers. A total of 49 victims were recorded at the scene, eight of whom were deceased."
Deadly road accidents are frequent in Brazil.
In February, a bus returning from a religious festival in northeast Brazil veered off the road and overturned, killing at least 16 people.
In October last year, 17 people died in northeast Brazil, in the state of Pernambuco, when a driver lost control of a bus.

Title: Tabung Haji weighs UK property exits as portfolio review begins [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   Tabung Haji is reviewing its exposure to property investments in the United Kingdom, including Great Minster House, as it maps out strategies to improve performance and address valuation gaps.
"We are reviewing our exposure to UK investments and are mapping out the appropriate strategy for each asset," Tabung Haji said in response to questions from
Business Times
.
The review includes measures to improve asset performance, address the gap between valuations and acquisition values and assess the timing and options for an orderly exit  deemed to be in Tabung Haji's best interest.
Great Minster House in 33, Horseferry Road, Victoria, central London, was acquired by a Tabung Haji subsidiary from Singapore-listed Sinarmas Land Ltd in 2022 for £247.5 million.
The six-storey freehold office building has about 180,000sq ft of space and is primarily occupied by the UK Department for Transport.
At the time of the acquisition, the property was leased to the UK government until 2033, providing Tabung Haji with a long-term income stream.
The acquisition was reportedly Tabung Haji's sixth UK property investment, according to its former group managing director, Datuk Seri Amrin Awaluddin.
At the time, Tabung Haji said the investment was expected to provide long-term returns through rental income and annual rental increases, while maintenance costs were borne by the tenant.
Tabung Haji's 2022 annual report said the investment was intended to diversify and expand its property portfolio.
The Great Minster House acquisition added to a UK property portfolio that Tabung Haji had been building since 2012.
UK property interests listed in the
fund's 2022 financial statements  include 10 Queen Street Place, Leatherhead Properties, Millstream Property  and others held through its UK subsidiaries.
The broader UK exposure has since come under scrutiny.
Tabung Haji chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain recently described the portfolio as a "legacy issue" that was "bleeding us", highlighting the need to address underperforming assets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says US scaling back military drills with South Korea
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Sunday he was "not happy" about US participation in joint military exercises with close ally South Korea and is scaling back the drills aimed at deterring rival North Korea that start Monday.
"Based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un, of North Korea, I am not happy with the fact that the United States has, long ago, agreed to participate in Joint Military Exercises with South Korea," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
"These exercises are not only costly, with much of these costs paid for by the United States of America (as usual!), but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, has been unthreatening and respectful," he continued.
Trump added that it was too late to cancel the drills so he had ordered Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to "substantially reduce" them.
The "Ulchi Freedom Shield" exercise, which starts on Monday and runs for 11 days, is a regular summer fixture for South Korea's armed forces and their US allies, designed to steel them for defence against the nuclear-armed North.
Pyongyang has always been angered by the drills, decrying them as dress rehearsals for an invasion.
During his first term as president, Trump held historic direct talks with Kim that ultimately failed in the goal of tackling North Korea's nuclear weapons programme. He last met with Kim in person in 2019.
Last Monday, Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean Combined Forces Command, said the exercise would simulate combat against North Korean troops battle-hardened by deployment in the Russia-Ukraine war.
The exercise – enlisting 18,000 South Korean troops and counterparts from the US contingent of 28,500 in the country – will have a heightened focus on drone warfare, GPS disruption and the role of cyber attacks, he said.
South Korea's dovish President Lee Jae Myung has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor since taking power in June 2025, offering Pyongyang talks without preconditions.
But the leadership of North Korea has yet to respond to his repeated offers.
The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 war, triggered by a North Korean attack, ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

Title: Trump welcomes defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Sunday he was pleased by the recent signing of a defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan.
"Very happy to see that Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan have recently, and finally, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement," he wrote on his Truth Social platform.
"It shows how the Middle East is coming together, and how Countries will finally be able to defend themselves in a more meaningful way," he wrote, calling it a "BIG, BOLD, IMPORTANT FIRST STEP."
The three-way agreement, signed Aug 7, comes amid a US-Iran war that has extended violence to the region, including Iran-backed Houthi rebel attacks.
Pakistan's foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was "intended to strengthen collective deterrence."
The agreement declared a "shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond."
The three countries will also share a commitment to participating in efforts to resolve the conflict between Iran and the United States.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: K.O.I strikes gold with 'Tiwikarma'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
FIRST-TIME finalist K.O.I made history at the 40th Anugerah Juara Lagu (AJL 40), turning an electrifying, theatrical performance of 'Tiwikarma' into a winning moment on Saturday night.
The hip-hop group captivated the judges with a dramatic performance at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil, overcoming strong contenders including Dayang Nurfaizah's 'Lemah' and Aina Abdul's 'Kamu' to take home the coveted grand trophy and RM100,000 cash prize.
Composed by Zai Hamzah and Hemo Globin, with lyrics penned by Achoi Floor 88, Khaza Raflex, Tuan Nicky, Mya Nana and Sapik Sam, 'Tiwikarma' proved a winning formula for K.O.I.
Group members were moved to tears as they expressed gratitude to those who had supported their musical journey.
Coming in second was Aisha Retno with 'Tak Adil', which she co-composed with Radi. She won a trophy and RM50,000.
Sabahan singer-songwriter Ryenald Guntabid took third place with 'Lumangad Oku Dika', winning RM30,000.
Marsha Milan clinched Best Vocals for 'Tangisan Seorang Pendosa', taking home RM12,000.
Aina Abdul won Best Performance and RM12,000 for her volcano-themed spectacle.
She was also crowned Shopee Choice Artist Icon, pocketing RM50,000 and earning the honour of representing Malaysia at Eurovision Asia 2026.
The trophies were presented by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, accompanied by Media Prima Bhd group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid, Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali and Media Prima Television Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof.
Chief judge Datuk Acis led the jury panel that featured SM Muzaffar, Efry, AG Coco, Siti Hajar, Ad Samad, LY, Pat Ibrahim and Helen Yap.
Hosted by Naz Rahman and Sissy Imann, with Fizi Ali and Fiza Frizzy handling red carpet and backstage coverage, AJL 40, with the theme "Love Your Legacy, Elevate Your Future", marked four decades of musical evolution.

Title: Malaysia braces for stronger El Nino, severe haze
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
WITH the heat tightening its grip and rainfall expected to remain scarce, Malaysia is preparing for a stronger El Niño that could bring a more severe haze.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the southwest monsoon intensified the phenomenon, bringing hotter, drier conditions and raising the risk of fires across the region.
He said the ministry had been monitoring the haze situation in Sarawak, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya since Aug 8, although conditions in the Klang Valley had improved.
He said three areas in Sarawak — Kuching, Samarahan and the Serian police headquarters — and Johan Setia in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of noon yesterday.
"The other areas recorded moderate API readings."
Kurup said preparations for El Niño and the southwest monsoon began with the National Haze and Dry Weather Committee's first meeting of the year on June 15.
State governments and agencies were briefed on the potential impact on agriculture, water supplies and reservoir levels.
He said measures would be carried out under the National Haze Action Plan and National Open Burning Action Plan, adding that Malaysia had stepped up regional coordination.
At meetings on transboundary haze pollution in Bali on July 8-9, Malaysia joined Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste in reviewing strategies to prevent forest and land fires.
Kurup also held bilateral discussions with Indonesia's environment minister to coordinate efforts to contain hotspots.
"Under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, Alert Level 2 was activated on Aug 3. Countries are required to submit daily reports on fires, haze and measures taken," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aussie state to start gun buyback on Nov 2
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
AUSTRALIA'S New South Wales state will start a gun buyback in November, said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese yesterday, as part of the national response to a shooting spree that killed 15 at a Jewish festival here.
Albanese's centre-left government enacted laws in January for the gun buyback, tighter checks for gun licences and a crackdown on hate in the wake of the Dec 14 attack at a Bondi Beach Hanukkah celebration in Australia's most populous city.
The alleged gunmen used legally obtained powerful firearms.
Australia had a record 4.1 million firearms last year, the government has said, with more than 1.1 million of those in New South Wales, its most populous state.
The buyback is to be the country's largest since a similar campaign after a 1996 massacre in Tasmania's Port Arthur, in which a gunman killed 35 people.
Albanese and New South Wales Premier Chris Minns said the scheme would start on Nov 2 and that people returning rifles and handguns would be eligible for up to A$1,000 compensation per firearm.
"Australians are quite rightly proud of our gun laws, but the fact is there are more guns in Australia today than there were at the time of dealing with the Port Arthur gun buyback," said Albanese in televised remarks.
New South Wales now limits each person to possession of four guns under its own reforms prompted by the Bondi Beach attack, which police say was by a father and son believed to be inspired by the Islamic State group.
The surviving suspect, Naveed Akram, 24, is yet to enter pleas to a raft of charges, including 15 counts of murder.

Title: SD Property tops out first Elmina high-rise
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd (SD Property) has topped out  Kanopi Residences, its first high-rise development in the 141.6ha Elmina City Centre in Sungai Buloh, Selangor.
This structural milestone keeps the development on track for completion in the third quarter of 2027.
The 36-storey project has a gross development value of RM299 million and comprises 499 units ranging from 550 to 1,200 square feet.
Located on Persiaran Garcinia near Elmina Lakeside Mall, Kanopi Residences is part of the City of Elmina masterplan and targets young professionals, first-time buyers and young families.
SD Property chief operating officer of township development Appollo Leong said the topping-out milestone reflected the company's commitment to delivering quality developments on schedule.
He said  the project supports a "15-minute city" concept, placing schools, shops and parks within a 15-minute walk or cycle ride.
Inspired by the neighbouring Bukit Cherakah Forest Reserve, Kanopi Residences adopts a nature-inspired concept, featuring more than 35 wellness and lifestyle facilities.
These include Co-Working in the Sky, Lounge in the Sky and Fitness in the Sky, alongside recreational and community facilities on Level 7.
The development connects to the Guthrie Corridor Expressway and Damansara-Shah Alam Elevated Expressway, while Elmina Lakeside Mall is about 300m  away.
Residents will also have access to the 121ha  Elmina Central Park, which has six theme parks linked by a 5km biodiversity corridor.
Kanopi Residences is also located near national and international schools.
Since its launch in the fourth quarter of 2024, the project has achieved a 90 per cent take-up rate, according to SD Property.
The project won a Gold Award for Best Lifestyle High-Rise Development  at the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Malaysia 2025.
SD Property said Kanopi Residences will expand the residential offering at Elmina City Centre and contribute to the development of sustainable, thriving communities.

Title: Trump's 2024 grocery photo op now haunts Republicans in the midterms
Article:
TWO years after Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump staged a New Jersey press conference flanked by grocery staples to spotlight inflation under Democrats, food prices are still rising despite his pledge to bring them down.
The gap between promise and reality now looms as a vulnerability for Republicans ahead of November's midterm elections.
Standing between tables piled high with fruit, beef, cereal, milk and other household staples at his Bedminster golf club on Aug 15, 2024, Trump blamed the Biden administration for sharp increases in groceries.
The spectacle, complete with charts showing higher prices, was aimed at undercutting the Democratic nominee, Kamala Harris, and highlighted Trump's central promise: he alone could tame inflation and lower the cost of living.
Two years on, higher gasoline and grocery prices are squeezing household budgets and turning the cost of living into the top issue for American voters.
Voters now give Democrats a slight edge over Republicans in who they view as better stewards of the economy for the first time in nearly a decade, according to Reuters/Ipsos polling.
Sheila Carney, a 68-year-old Trump voter, punctuated her frustration with an expletive as she unloaded US$70 worth of groceries into her car outside a supermarket not far from Trump's Bedminster club.
The haul was modest: some meat, detergent and a 12-pack of iced tea.
For Carney, the receipt was evidence that the affordability concerns Trump has sometimes dismissed as a Democratic "hoax" remain a daily burden for many Americans.
"This is real. He can say it's not, but it is," said Carney, a hospital administration assistant who has delayed retirement while helping pay off her son's student loans.
"He hasn't brought anything down."
A Reuters analysis of 26 grocery categories tracked by the Bureau of Labor Statistics and featured in Trump's Bedminster display found prices have risen 3.4 per cent in the first 19 months of his second term.
That's less than a quarter of the pace recorded at the same point in former President Joe Biden's term, but still falls short of Trump's pledge to lower prices, as surges in coffee, beef and apples have more than offset declines in items including eggs and butter.
[[nid:1512622]]
A White House official pointed to data on Wednesday that showed US consumer prices barely increased in July from the month before as evidence that inflation is under control.
"The July CPI report is further proof that President Trump's long-term agenda is delivering: prescription drug and auto insurance costs continue to fall, real wages are rising, and beef prices have cooled while other household essentials like eggs, poultry, and dairy remain low," the official said.
A registered Republican, Carney said high grocery and gasoline prices due to the Iran war were among the reasons she had grown disillusioned enough to consider sitting out the midterms, underscoring recent polling suggesting Republicans are less enthusiastic about voting than Democrats.
Carney was one of 17 Republicans and independents Reuters interviewed in New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, a battleground that includes Bedminster and where swing voters and turnout could prove decisive.
The race pits Republican incumbent Tom Kean against Democrat Rebecca Bennett, who has sought to capitalise on voters' frustration over the cost of living.
More than half of those interviewed said they were either undecided or leaning toward Bennett. While grocery prices weighed heavily on many voters, complaints about Kean more often centred on his months-long disappearance from public view earlier this year, which he later attributed to depression.
Their views on the economy mirror those of other Trump supporters Reuters has interviewed in recent months who, despite standing by the president, say financial pressures have dampened their enthusiasm for voting in November.
That ambivalence presents another potential challenge for Republicans and raises the stakes for the party's get-out-the-vote operation.
Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley, recently co-authored research finding that Trump drew stronger support in the 2024 election in counties where inflation outpaced income growth, eroding households' purchasing power.
With real wages rising only marginally and lagging the pace of broader economic growth, Trebbi said it is likely that pattern will reverse in November.
"I expect the same anti-incumbent shift to happen in 2026, this time possibly weakening Republicans," he said, describing grocery shopping as a "psychologically salient" reminder of the squeeze on household finances.
"Each time one does it, it is the equivalent of a campaign ad against the incumbent."
To be sure, presidents have limited influence over inflation, which is driven by a range of factors and more directly addressed by the Federal Reserve. And many Republicans appear willing to give Trump the benefit of the doubt, even as his tariffs and the Iran war have contributed to rising prices.
Bonnie Chandler, 64, plans to vote for Kean, saying she believed some companies were keeping prices elevated to make Trump look bad and that the growing influence of the Democratic Party's progressive faction left her unwilling to consider its candidates.
"I'm going to vote Republican. I'm not a woke person. I'm not a communist. I'm not a socialist," she said.
[[nid:1512621]]
Lauren DeGirolamo, a 34-year-old Trump voter, said issues such as education and border security mattered more to her than grocery prices, which she believes have stabilised under Trump following steep increases during the Biden administration.
"I feel grocery prices are pretty much at level with where they were during Biden. I know some of the key things that I look for - eggs - have gone down," she said, adding that she intended to vote for Republican candidates in November.
According to BLS data, egg prices have fallen nearly 40 per cent under Trump, reflecting a market correction after avian flu-driven shortages triggered a surge that began during Biden's presidency.
Eggs are among six of the 26 categories showing falls since 2025, along with butter, bacon, and cooking fats and oils.
Yet most of the items Trump displayed at Bedminster are now pricier, some by a lot. Uncooked beef has jumped 19.2 per cent, fresh fish and seafood 8.6 per cent, apples 14 per cent, and coffee nearly 23 per cent.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll that concluded earlier this month found Trump's net approval rating on his handling of the cost of living was at -47 per cent, down from -6 per cent at the start of his term. It is his weakest issue by a wide margin, trailing his ratings on the economy (-35 per cent) and immigration (-16 per cent).
Bennett told Reuters that if elected she would seek to undo Trump's tariffs, rein in the Iran war, and restore food stamp benefits to help families struggling to afford groceries.
The issue hits close to home, said Bennett, a military veteran and married mother of two daughters.
"This is not an abstract concept to me," she said. "For example, beef is very expensive, so we don't buy beef anymore."
Whether Kean, whose campaign did not respond to requests for comment, can hold on to his seat may depend on voters like Margaret Derkach, who typically votes Republican but is now considering switching her vote if economic conditions don't improve.
"The cost of living, as far as homes, apartments and food - the necessities - they have gone up. It's shocking, shocking," said Derkach, 84, after shopping at discount grocer Aldi.
Though she said Trump "inherited a mess" from Biden, Derkach added, "I am undecided right now. I have to see."
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Rafizi: Bersama is not Trojan horse for BN, Pas to defeat PH
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) is not a Trojan horse serving the interests of Barisan Nasional and Pas, Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said.
Rafizi dismissed claims that Bersama was established as an agent to undermine Pakatan Harapan, particularly DAP and PKR, describing the allegations as unfounded.
"There are people saying Bersama is actually a Trojan horse, a good friend of Zahid Hamidi (Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi) and Sanusi (Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor), to destroy DAP and PKR.
"BN and Pas do not need an agent to defeat PH," he said during a Bersama gathering here last night.
He said Bersama did not need to act as an agent for BN or Pas to defeat PH, arguing that existing political dynamics were already sufficient.
Rafizi said the "Trojan horse" narrative reflected how established political parties viewed Bersama's emergence rather than the party's actual purpose.
He also took aim at Umno and Pas for what he described as their continued reliance on racial and religious politics, saying the approach failed to address the country's underlying problems.
He claimed both parties continued to revolve around the same political narratives instead of offering solutions to issues affecting ordinary Malaysians, including the cost of living, healthcare and incomes.
"Why do they keep circling around the same things? They will talk about race, they will talk about religion. They never talk about the real issues we face," he said.
Rafizi said the country's political landscape had changed significantly and that approaches that might have worked decades ago could no longer adequately address Malaysia's challenges.
He alleged that Umno and Pas would continue exploiting Malay, Bumiputera and Muslim sentiments because Malaysia's demographic composition would increasingly favour the Bumiputera population.
He said this would make race-based politics an increasingly powerful electoral tool unless there was a credible alternative capable of convincing Malay and Bumiputera voters that their interests could be protected without relying on racial mobilisation.
He said the answer should be a political approach centred on competence and integrity rather than race.
"We need to convince Malay and Bumiputera voters that what will help Malays, Bumiputera, Chinese, Indians, Iban and Kadazan is not political power.
"What we need is to ensure that whoever is elected must be competent and have integrity, regardless of whether he is Malay, Chinese or Indian," he said.
Rafizi said Umno and Pas had benefited politically from the failure of other parties to develop such an alternative.
He argued that when non-Malay voters were encouraged to rally behind DAP out of fear of Umno and Pas, it could inadvertently reinforce the very racial divide that both sides claimed to oppose.
"The more you talk like that, the more Umno and Pas will respond: 'That is why you need to support us'," he said.
Rafizi also criticised what he described as the tendency of Umno and Pas to exploit public dissatisfaction through populist narratives rather than confront difficult policy questions.
He said the same criticism applied to PH parties, which he accused of repeatedly relying on nostalgia and familiar political narratives rather than presenting a convincing long-term direction.
Rafizi said this cycle could eventually strengthen racial and religious politics, with Umno and Pas positioning themselves as defenders of Malay interests while DAP sought to rally non-Malay voters by presenting itself as their last line of defence.
"The result is going back to politics based on race because it becomes us versus them," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR has changed approach, now wants dissenters back, says Rafizi
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said PKR's recent congress reflected a change in the party's political approach.
Rafizi said PKR leaders previously appeared quick to tell dissenting members to leave, but its recent congress saw calls for former members to return.
"Before this, whenever PKR had a function, its leaders were very strong. They would say, 'Anyone who disagrees with us in the party, please leave.' And they really left.
"But at this year's congress, did you hear anyone telling them to leave? (PKR president Datuk Seri) Anwar (Ibrahim) was appealing for them to come back. Things have changed," he said in his speech during a gathering with Bersama members in Penang last night.
Rafizi also took aim at Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil's admission at the congress that PKR had a communication problem with the public.
He said the admission was significant as the issue had been raised repeatedly over the years.
"I saw Fahmi Fadzil admit that we actually have a problem communicating with the people. People have been saying this for years," he said.
However, Rafizi questioned whether acknowledging the problem amounted to taking responsibility, pointing out that Fahmi did not offer to resign over the matter.
"If he had finished by saying, 'As such, I take responsibility and resign,' then fine. But he did not resign," he added.
Rafizi also criticised a delegate who highlighted PKR's past struggles, saying the party appeared to be relying heavily on nostalgia instead of addressing its future direction.
He said PKR had repeatedly revisited its history whenever it faced difficulties rather than presenting a clear way forward.
"Every time they have a problem, they have to rely on nostalgia. They talk about nostalgia, stories from the past, again and again," he said.
Rafizi said the congress should instead have focused on problems facing ordinary Malaysians, including the cost of living, healthcare and other everyday concerns.
He said political parties could no longer rely on approaches that worked decades ago, as Malaysia's society and economic circumstances had changed significantly.

Title: DAP unlikely to quit govt before GE16, says Rafizi
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli claimed DAP was unlikely to leave the government after having tasted power.
Rafizi said DAP's extensive representation in government, from ministers and deputy ministers to state executive councillors, elected representatives and local councillors, made it difficult for the party to walk away despite disagreements within Pakatan Harapan.
"Once you have tasted power, if in Penang someone has become a city councillor, do you think it is easy for them to let go?" he asked.
He said DAP's involvement in government extended to thousands of positions, making it unrealistic to expect its members to simply vote to leave the administration based on political principles.
"DAP has positions from full ministers, deputy ministers, chief ministers, exco members, elected representatives, councillors and further down, village heads. Thousands of people," he said during a gathering with Bersama members in Penang last night.
Rafizi said claims that DAP's special congress could result in the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan-led government were therefore misplaced.
He said DAP would remain in government until the next general election, despite the party's deliberations on its position in the coalition.
Yesterday, DAP delegates voted overwhelmingly to remain in the Unity Government, with 88 per cent choosing to stay in the Cabinet for the remainder of the parliamentary term.
The result, with 1,857 votes in favour of remaining and 242 against, was reached during the party's special congress.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke had said that the outcome represented a clear mandate for the party leadership to press on with its reform agenda within the government.
In his speech, Rafizi claimed DAP remained tied to a racial politics narrative, saying the party must move beyond it and offer a forward-looking alternative.
He said DAP appeared increasingly constrained by its reliance on its traditional support base and was unable to articulate a convincing way forward following its special congress.
He said the party should instead convince Malaysians of all races that race should not be viewed as a threat to one another, while competent and clean leadership should be the basis for choosing a government.
"The antidote to the politics of Umno and Pas is to convince Malays, Chinese, Indians, Ibans and Kadazans that race is not a threat to each other," he added.
Rafizi said DAP's challenge was that it could not simply promote Pakatan Harapan as a coalition of leaders with integrity and expertise without addressing problems that had emerged during the current administration.
"Why can't DAP say, 'Choose Pakatan Harapan because we are the ones with integrity, expertise and the skills to solve the country's problems?'" he asked.
He said DAP's continued emphasis on defending non-Malay interests could inadvertently strengthen race-based politics by reinforcing an "us versus them" narrative.
Rafizi said the party's response to the growing influence of Umno and Pas should not be to deepen communal divisions, but to demonstrate that competent and trustworthy leadership could serve Malaysians regardless of race.
He said DAP's direction following its special congress would therefore be significant in determining whether Malaysia's political discourse continued to revolve around race and religion or shifted towards addressing structural problems.

Title: Four prized Renaissance works stolen from museum in Sicily
Article:
ROME: Four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina have been stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said Sunday.
The theft, that includes three panels of the 15th century San Gregorio Polyptych, occurred late Saturday at a museum in Messina, the religious painter's hometown.
The theft comes just months after the Italian state bought a work called "Ecce Homo" by Antonello da Messina at a New York auction in New York for nearly US$15 million (13 million euros).
Messina mayor Federico Basile called the theft "deeply reprehensible", saying it was "even more painful" as it took place during traditional city celebrations in honour of the Virgin Mary.
Art thefts are frequent in Italy.
Italian police two days ago said they had recovered three paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth over nine million euros (US$10.4 million) that had been stolen from a museum near Parma in northern Italy in March, allegedly by a gang of Moldovans.--AFp
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR congress ends, but reformasi fight goes on, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 PKR National Congress has renewed the party's resolve to advance its reform agenda and strengthen its machinery to ensure its struggle continues to benefit the people, said PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the two-day congress, which concluded today, was not merely a platform for speeches and debates, but also an opportunity for self-reflection, listening to the grassroots, assessing the party's strengths and weaknesses, and renewing its commitment to its cause.
He said PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's address served as a clear reminder that the "reformasi" struggle must continue and that the party's strength must always be anchored in the interests of the people.
"We return to our respective constituencies and reconnect with the people, listen to their views, understand their concerns, and keep finding ways to solve the problems they face. We must also strengthen our organisation and move as a disciplined team.
"Political challenges will continue to come, but Keadilan must remain steadfast in its principles and the people's struggle agenda," he said in a Facebook post.
Fahmi added that although the congress had ended, the responsibility of the party machinery continued, with members needing to work harder, listen and ensure that the struggle continuously brought tangible benefits.

Title: Flores quake survivors cling to hope amid destruction
Article:
MELANIA  Nius was at her husband's hospital bedside on Indonesia's Flores island when a powerful quake shook their town to its core, sending patients fleeing into the chaos outside.
Melania, 56, recounted how she prayed as she fought to get her family to safety.
"The four of us — my husband, our two children, and I were on the bed" when the 7.7-magnitude rattler stuck just north of the island about 5.30am on Saturday.
Forty-eight people were killed in the quake, and dozens injured.
"The bed almost flipped over. Tables and all the things on the tables and on top of the cupboards all fell and scattered everywhere," she said.
"We were panicking. When the shaking eased a little, we immediately pushed his bed and took him outside."
Her husband Basianus Cak was being treated on the hospital's third floor for a heart and lung condition and diabetes.
Melania said debris partly blocked the evacuation route, but they made their way out with the help of others.
"I just prayed: 'God, if you still give us the chance to live, please open a way for us'," she said.
"Thank God, he has given us another chance to live."
The epicentre of the shallow quake was just north of Flores island in eastern Indonesia.
The area hardest hit was Nagekeo, around 200km east of Ruteng.
About 5,000 Flores inhabitants evacuated and authorities issued an initial tsunami warning that was later lifted.
Most stayed outside overnight as more than 300 aftershocks threatened to bring down compromised buildings. Dozens of patients were moved on Saturday to tents erected outside the Ruteng hospital, many with their loved ones by their side.
Tonsianus Sambang was visiting his mother, being treated for a ruptured blood vessel in her brain, when the quake struck.
"So, we all started to panic. Some people jumped out of windows, and some ran outside," said the 31-year-old as he stroked his mother's leg under her hospital blanket.
"Things were falling everywhere, so our main priority at that moment was how to evacuate the patients and get them out of that room.
"The walls were collapsing, debris was falling, and objects were scattered across the floor."
Tonsianus said he was "very worried" about aftershocks and about his mother and other patients having to sleep outside.
He made an appeal to the government  to bring medical supplies and other aid as quickly as possible.
The hospital also has to deal with an influx of people injured in the quake, like Yoktafiana Sinar whose house came down on top of her.
"The wound on my head is getting better, but my leg still hurts. It was broken when the house collapsed on me," said the restaurant worker, 40.
"It was at six in the morning. I was about to take a shower and get ready for work when the earthquake struck.
"I shielded my grandchild under my stomach, and I was the one who was hit when the house collapsed," said Yoktafiana.
Emergency officials said on Sunday at least 914 houses were severely damaged in the quake and hundreds of others to a lesser degree.
Dozens of public facilities were also stricken, including 93 educational and 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to thousands of people in temporary shelters.
The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc's Copernicus Earth observation satellites.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Saudi Arabia issues alert for Jazan province along Yemen border
Article:
RIYADH: The Saudi civil defence agency issued an alert on Sunday warning of "potential danger" in southern Jazan province along the border with Yemen that has been targeted by Yemeni rebels recently.
"A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in the Jazan Province to alert of a potential danger," read the statement by the agency, with similar alerts usually issued ahead of potential strikes targeting an area.
The Teheran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have repeatedly targeted energy and petroleum installations in Jazan in recent weeks.
A years-long truce in Yemen's civil war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government appeared to collapse last month as fighting between regional allies of the United States and Iran flared.
The breakdown of the UN-backed 2022 accord came as the Houthi rebels announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and the kingdom's oil infrastructure, which comes with Iran blockading the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.
The Houthis control vast swathes of Yemen, including the capital Sanaa and areas on the border with Saudi Arabia's Red Sea provinces.--AFP

Title: 23 students to undergo eye misalignment surgery at HPUSM
Article:
KOTA BARU: Twenty-three students aged between seven and 19 will undergo surgery for strabismus, or eye misalignment, at Universiti Sains Malaysia Specialist Hospital (HPUSM) over five days, helping to reduce a waiting period that could previously stretch from several months to years.
HPUSM director Datuk Dr Ab Rahman Izani Ghani @ Ab Ghani said the surgeries were being carried out in conjunction with the second Strabismus Surgery Carnival, which runs from today until Aug 20.
He said the students were identified through HPUSM's Short-sightedness and Strabismus Eye Intervention Programme, which was conducted at schools throughout Kelantan over the past three years.
"Through the screening, HPUSM identified about 300 students with eye problems, including strabismus, and 23 of them will undergo surgery during the five-day carnival.
"This is a significant achievement as it helps reduce the waiting period, which previously could take several months and, in some cases, years," he told reporters after launching the second Strabismus Surgery Carnival at HPUSM here today.
The carnival brings together ophthalmology consultants specialising in strabismus surgery, ophthalmologists and postgraduate ophthalmology students to provide assessment and surgical treatment.
He said the cost of the surgeries was funded by the Kelantan Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council  and several non-governmental organisations.
Meanwhile, USM School of Medical Sciences paediatric ophthalmology consultant Professor Dr Shatriah Ismail said strabismus was not merely a cosmetic issue, as it could affect visual function, eye coordination and psychological development, particularly among children.
She said the condition could also affect patients' self-confidence and ability to adapt to daily life.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hamas expects meeting with Kushner as US pushes Gaza plan
Article:
CAIRO: Hamas sources said on Sunday that they expected to meet in Egypt with US envoy Jared Kushner, as President Donald Trump's administration seeks to push forward a Gaza peace plan rejected by Israel.
Two weeks after Hamas publicly signed on to the latest phase of the deal, Kushner, who is Trump's son-in-law and special envoy, flew to Egypt ahead of expected talks on Monday in Jerusalem.
"Mediators informed Hamas that US envoy Jared Kushner will hold a meeting with the Hamas leadership, in the presence of Egyptian and Qatari officials, before Kushner travels to Israel to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu," a Hamas source told AFP, requesting anonymity to discuss sensitive diplomacy.
Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya traveled late Saturday to the Egyptian Mediterranean city of El-Alamein in his first trip since taking over the Gaza-based movement last month.
A second Hamas source said that the United States had sought clarifications from Hamas on several points including on "genuine, rather than merely symbolic, collection, consolidation and storage of weapons, as well as Hamas's complete relinquishment of governance of Gaza."
Hamas on July 30 said that it would hand over its weapons to a new Palestinian governing body as part of the latest stage in a Gaza ceasefire declared by Trump, who hailed their agreement as a "major milestone."
But Netanyahu, a longtime hawk who faces a tough re-election fight in October, said that Israel rejected the agreement and voiced scepticism that Hamas would actually give up its weapons.
Netanyahu voiced opposition to the plan even after he was assured by Nickolay Mladenov, the Gaza high representative in Trump's "Board of Peace" set up to implement the deal, that Israel would not need to pull troops out of the Gaza Strip until complete disarmament by Hamas.
The board had initially said that Israel would start a phased withdrawal in tandem with Hamas's disarmament.
The United States for years refused contact with Hamas, which led the Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel that sparked the Gaza war.
But the Trump administration has increasingly been comfortable with direct contact in hopes of ending the devastating war, negotiating the October ceasefire agreement that led to the release of remaining Israeli hostages.
There was no immediate confirmation of a meeting between Kushner and Hamas by the United States.
A Board of Peace official earlier said that Kushner and Mladenov hoped for "constructive conversations" with Netanyahu, and that "the United States and Israel agree on the end state, which is a demilitarised Hamas."
- ISRAEL KEEPS UP STRIKES -
Kushner discussed the Gaza plan with Egyptian  President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi during a meeting that "emphasised the need for all parties to fulfill their obligations under the Gaza Strip ceasefire agreement", according to presidential spokesperson Mohamed El-Shennawy.
Hamas's Al-Hayaa met on Sunday with Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad and "reaffirmed commitment" to the Trump plan, Egypt's state-run Middle East News Agency said.
A Hamas official had told AFP the delegation would brief Egypt on Israeli violations of the ceasefire agreement.
Israel has resumed airstrikes in Gaza after a lull following Trump's promotion of the peace plan, though the October ceasefire had never fully halted the violence in the Strip.
Several people were injured Sunday after Israeli aircraft targeted a house west of Nuseirat, said Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency, which serves as a rescue service under Hamas.
The Israeli military said it was responding to a threat by Islamic Jihad fighters and that it tried to mitigate civilian casualties.
"The group's advanced attacks and were struck in precise aerial strikes to remove the threat," it said.
Several others were injured after Israeli forces opened fire on tents housing displaced people west of Khan Yunis, where separately the body of a child, Suhail Shallouf, was recovered after he was killed by Israeli fire on Saturday, the civil defence agency said.
Israeli operations have killed at least 1,262 Palestinians since the ceasefire came into effect on Oct 10, according to figures by Gaza's health ministry, which is under Hamas. Its figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.--AFP

Title: Gold shines as confidence in reserve assets fades
Article:
GOLD is on the rise again, as a confluence of economic and political dynamics spurs demand from investors around the world, especially one cohort: central banks.
After stalling around US$4,000 an ounce for several weeks, bullion has jumped around US$400, or 10 per cent, since the start of this month and could be on track for its best month this century.
The last time it rose 13 per cent or more in a month was September 1999. There have been a few key United States-related triggers for the spike, namely the Federal Reserve's  "dovish hold" on interest rates, weak employment data, and fairly tame inflation figures.
These have all tempered Fed rate hike expectations and dragged down the US dollar — manna for gold.
But they come against a more unnerving geopolitical and policy backdrop that has reminded the world of gold's underlying appeal, particularly for reserve managers.
The US-Iran war has re-escalated, and hopes of a peace "deal" — however unsatisfactory that deal might be — are evaporating. US President Donald Trump's off-ramp ahead of November's midterm elections is narrowing.
Escalation or capitulation is not the only choices Trump faces, but it is a black-and-white scenario some analysts are now beginning to contemplate.
Meanwhile, doubts about the Fed's independence and chair Kevin Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility are growing.
Investors weren't impressed by his remarks last month about the central bank's two per cent inflation goal. Furthermore, media reports suggest Trump has repeatedly called Warsh since his appointment, and Trump has revived his attempts to fire Governor Lisa Cook.
All this has unnerved the bond market. Yields on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note have climbed to their highest level in 18 months, while yields on 30-year bonds and 30-year inflation-protected bonds are at their highest since 2007 and 2008, respectively.
Little wonder, perhaps, that central banks have continued to reduce their Treasuries held in custody at the New York Fed. These are the lowest since 2012.
"The US is now in a phase where its global seigniorage benefits of supplying the world's reserve currency have now been exhausted; the next phase (which may already be underway) is what happens when the foreign official holders of your liabilities become more antsy about holding them," economist Phil Suttle wrote last week.
None of these events on their own would necessarily spark a huge revival in gold. But throw them all together, and it's a pretty compelling checklist.
Especially for central banks, which had already started to ramp up their purchases in the second quarter after a lacklustre first quarter.
Net purchases by central banks in the April-June period totalled 289 tonnes, more than five times the volume of the prior three months, according to the World Gold Council.
This was a record high for a second quarter. Taking the average price into account, analysts at Deutsche Bank estimate second-quarter central bank demand was a record US$45 billion.
That record may be broken soon. A WGC survey of central banks in June showed that a record 45 per cent of respondents plan to increase their gold holdings over the next 12 months.
Initial hard numbers appear to back that up. China's central bank bought a net 20 tonnes last month, a rise of 0.9 per cent from the previous month. That was the biggest increase, by both measures, since October 2023, lifting its total gold reserves to a record 2,377.5 tonnes.
"China is again adding materially to its reserves. Gold is not a pure Fed signal, but persistent official-sector demand and renewed investor interest are reinforcing the value of inflation, currency and geopolitical hedges," BNY analysts wrote.
But central banks move slowly, and a clear picture of their reacquaintance with bullion won't emerge for some months. It probably won't be a one-way street either.
An International Monetary Fund paper last month found that gold is "highly volatile, offers only conditional hedging and diversification benefits", and shouldn't be bought for liquidity purposes.
"Central banks should treat gold as a high-risk reserve asset and anchor gold accumulation decisions in strategic asset allocation and sound policy analysis," said the authors.
Central banks are unlikely to chase the rally blindly. But as confidence in the world's reserve assets frays, gold's allure is unlikely to dim.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two dead, hundreds evacuated from fires on island near Athens
Article:
ATHENS: Two people died and hundreds were evacuated Sunday after two fires broke out on the Greek island of Salamis near Athens, the fire department said.
A fire department spokesman told AFP that "two bodies were recovered" from the Peristeria beach area in the south of the island, as the service announced that hundreds of people had hurriedly been evacuated an hour earlier.
"There are hundreds of bathers and permanent residents, an evacuation order has been issued," the service's deputy spokesman Yiannis Artopios told state TV ERT.
The civil protection ministry issued four evacuation orders in short succession as the fires broke out "almost simultaneously" in Peristeria and Selinia, two popular beaches in the island's south and east, Artopios said.
"It is a difficult fire... inside an inhabited area," he said.
Some roads remained open and police forces were on hand to guide them to safety, Artopios said.
Nine people required medical care for burns, state agency ANA said.
Salamis, just west of Athens, has some 37,000 residents, many of them elderly, and the beaches were full of people on Sunday, officials said.
Local officials were trying to keep the fire in Selinia from scaling a mountain and linking up with the other fire, Salamina deputy mayor Thodoris Zannis told the station.
The fire was burning through pine forest and bush, officials said.
The fire service mobilised a large force of some 200 firefighters, nearly 50 engines, six aircraft and seven helicopters, rushing in reinforcements from the mainland, Artopios said.
Greece's coastguard said it had dispatched seven patrol boats to the area and several other private vessels including ferries were being made available.
"So far around 90 people have been evacuated by sea," coastguard spokesman Theofanis Balatsoukas told ERT.
"(The operation) is proceeding smoothly," he said.
The fire department also had two vessels assisting, Artopios said.
- SKYROS BLAZE CONTAINED -
After largely escaping the heatwave temperatures that blanketed much of Europe earlier this summer, Greece has been hit with several major wildfires since late July, fuelled by unusually strong winds.
Firefighters had largely contained a blaze on the Aegean island of Skyros earlier, an AFP reporter said.
Thirty-four fires have broken out over the past 24 hours around the country, according to the fire department.
Five firefighters have died so far, including a Danish pilot killed in a mid-air collision between two Bell helicopters while battling a blaze near Athens earlier this month.
Winds were expected to ease later Sunday. According to the civil protection ministry, on Monday for the first time in 10 days, no area was above 3 on the national fire risk scale, which runs to 5, its highest level.
Greece is hit by wildfires every year.
Experts say the risk is growing because of human-fuelled climate change, which has made droughts and other extreme weather event more severe.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Auku's abolition must usher in better regulation
Article:
THE abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) is a welcome and significant reform, but its real test will be what fills the vacuum. The government must be praised for being willing to move away from legislation that has long been associated with restrictions on academic and student freedom.
From day one, Auku was a target of criticism. Over the 55 years of its life, it has been a patchwork of amendments. Even in the year the act was passed, it was amended.
The latest was in 2024, bringing the total to seven amendments. Perhaps the most significant amendment was in 2012, allowing students to join activities organised by political parties outside campus.
But abolition will mean little if its restrictive provisions simply reappear through administrative rules. This means that universities may have to rely much more heavily on their own statutes, regulations and governance mechanisms.
While this is an opportunity, it is also a test of institutional maturity. Autonomy cannot mean universities simply inherit Auku's powers through internal regulations. Universities should not be allowed to reproduce restrictive practices under a different name.
Academic freedom must come with academic responsibility. Greater freedom does not mean absence of standards. Universities still need mechanisms to deal with misconduct, harassment, discrimination and behaviour that genuinely threatens the safety and integrity of the institution.
Universities will do well to have a binding comprehensive policy covering sexual harassment, bullying, disability discrimination and abuse of authority by lecturers, supervisors or administrators.
This is obviously not an exhaustive list. It can only be comprehensive if the policies and rules cover everyone employed by the universities and students.
Importantly, the policies and rules must cover situations where there is a power imbalance. And also where there is concentration of power, like in the university administrators, who act as the complainants, prosecutors, judges and appeal authorities.
Experts have long called for the separation of investigation from punishment. If reasons are needed, the move to separate the roles of the attorney-general and the public prosecutor provides many, the main reason being to avoid conflict of interest.
Justice must not only be done but must be seen to be done is an old legal principle. The end of Auku should not mark the end of regulation. It should mark the beginning of better regulation that is closer to the universities, more transparent, fairer and less vulnerable to abuse of power.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman who died after headscarf became entangled in water gate roller laid to rest
Article:
SUNGAI BESAR: Department of Irrigation and Drainage worker Selaton Nuri, who died after her headscarf became entangled in the roller of a water gate yesterday, was buried tonight.
The remains of the 55-year-old mother of six underwent a post-mortem at Sungai Buloh Hospital before being washed and shrouded.
The remains were then taken to her home in Kampung Bagan Terap about 5.30pm
for her family to pay their last respects before being brought to Al-Mujahiddin Mosque in Pekan Bagan Terap for funeral prayers.
The funeral prayers were led by her 26-year-old son, Riduan Basar.
After the prayers, the remains were taken to the Kampung Bagan Terap Muslim Cemetery and buried about 9.40pm.
It was previously reported that Selaton was involved in
the tragedy
while attempting to close a water gate following a high tide.
Sabak Bernam district police chief Superintendent Md Yusof Ahmad was reported to have said that police received information about the incident at 4pm and classified the case as
sudden death.

Title: Iran offers US$30,000 bounty for killing, capturing US soldiers
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's military announced on Sunday that it was offering a bounty equivalent to US$30,000 for killing or capturing US soldiers, with the reward doubled if carried out by a woman.
Army chief Amir Hatami said the plan had been drawn up following a "large number of requests" to participate, according to the IRNA state news agency.
There has been no known deployment of US ground forces in Iran during the Middle East war, with the exception of a rescue mission in April for a downed American airman.
Hatami did not provide any details on where or when the killing or capturing of US soldiers was expected to take place.
"Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to US$30,000 or 5 billion tomans from the Islamic Republic of Iran's Army," Hatami said, using an informal unit equivalent to 10,000 Iranian rials.
"Courageous Iranian women who carry out such an action will receive double the reward," he added.
Hatami repeated Iran's call for the US to leave the Middle East, and said "they no longer have permission to enter the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Oman or the Strait of Hormuz."
The war between Teheran and Washington began on Feb 28 when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.
Just over a month into the war, the US launched a massive rescue operation to retrieve the weapon systems officer of an F-15 jet, involving around 200 US troops and more than 170 aircraft racing to find the airman ahead of Iranian forces.
During the rescue, Iranian troops damaged an A-10 ground attack aircraft which was ditched over friendly territory. The US also reportedly abandoned and destroyed aircraft used during the mission including a C-130 transport plane.
Days before, the pilot of the F-15 was rescued by a helicopter crew in a smaller operation.
The war was later paused by an April ceasefire after nearly 40 days of fighting, followed by a June framework for peace talks that later collapsed.
Iran and the United States have since traded fire sporadically, with fighting mainly centred in southern Iran and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Indirect contact between the two sides via mediators has continued with little sign of any diplomatic breakthrough. Iran has also set out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including war damages.
The number of US military personnel killed since the start of the war stands at 17, with the most recent deaths in July. They have all been killed outside of Iran, in countries including Jordan and Iraq. --AFP

Title: 15-year-old student dies after motorcycle crashes into trailer
Article:
PENDANG: A secondary school student died after the motorcycle he was riding was involved in an accident with another motorcycle and a trailer along Jalan By Pass here today.
The 15-year-old student of SMK Pendang suffered severe head injuries and died at the scene.
District police chief Superintendent Rodzi Abu Hassan said police received a report on the accident about 1.40pm.
"Preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred when the trailer driver, who was travelling from Kuala Kedah towards Padang Pusing, signalled and stopped on the left road shoulder after experiencing numbness in his leg.
"The trailer driver then heard a loud crash from behind and found that the motorcycle ridden by the victim had crashed into the right side of the trailer before being thrown towards the road divider," he said when contacted today.
Rodzi said at the same time, another motorcycle ridden by a male student was unable to brake in time and crashed into the victim.
"The accident was caused by the trailer being parked on the left road shoulder without the necessary warning signals," he said.
Rodzi said a preliminary urine screening test on the trailer lorry driver was negative for drugs and he was detained for investigation under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Government to amend Tabung Haji Act 1995, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be safeguarded, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the amendment was among the Madani Government's measures to strengthen governance and ensure that institutional weaknesses were addressed firmly.
"Governance must continue to be strengthened, institutions cleaned up and every weakness firmly addressed.
"The Tabung Haji Act will be amended to safeguard the trust of Muslims.
"… meanwhile, AUKU (Universities and University Colleges Act) 1971 must be completely repealed without being replaced by a new law that continues to restrict students' voices," he said in a Facebook post today.
In the same post, Anwar said the unity government under his leadership would continue to ensure that economic growth translated into a better quality of life for the people, regardless of their political affiliation or state of residence.
He said people in opposition-led states also deserved to be looked after, as the government's responsibility was not only towards its supporters or certain states, but the entire population and nation.
Following the conclusion of the 2026 PKR National Congress today, Anwar, who is also the PKR president, said the party had chosen the path of principles, idealism and courage to do what was right, without compromising its principles or betraying the ideals of Reformasi simply to retain power.
He stressed that PKR must remain a platform for all Malaysians, transcending race, religion and region, with the principle of justice demonstrated through policies and actions.
"PKR's strength relies on a clean team, strong leadership and organised efforts. Strength is not a tool to enrich oneself, one's family or cronies, but a trust to champion the people, uphold justice and elevate human dignity.
"Close ranks, streamline efforts and continue moving forward for the people and the nation," he said.

Title: Kelantan royal crown goes on public display for first time
Article:
KOTA BARU: A centuries-old symbol of Kelantan's royalty is stepping into the public spotlight for the first time, with the Kelantan royal crown going on display at the Heritage Weapons Festival here.
The 21-day festival, which begins today, is being held at Istana Balai Besar and will feature the rare royal regalia among its main attractions.
Kelantan Sultan's Office protocol officer Mohamed Safaruddin Ismail said the crown was one of the state's most significant royal artefacts and a symbol of the sovereignty of the Kelantan Sultanate.
He said Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V had consented to the crown being displayed publicly, giving visitors a rare opportunity to see it up close.
"For those who have never seen the crown, this is a rare opportunity. We invite the public to come and see it for themselves.
"The exhibition is not only about weapons but also about preserving and introducing Kelantan's rich royal and cultural heritage to the public," he said when met.
Safaruddin said the festival would also showcase about 250 traditional weapons, including kelewang, parang jambu, badik Kelantan, axes, lawi ayam, lawi itik and various types of keris.
[[nid:1512536]]
"The collection will also include manuscripts, traditional artefacts and Kelantan currency, making this an exhibition that offers something for everyone," he added.
He said the festival, held from Aug 16 to Sept 5, was expected to attract about 50,000 visitors, surpassing the 42,000 recorded during last year's Textile and Kelantan Heritage Festival.
Safaruddin said the festival attracted about 30,000 visitors in 2024, with organisers now setting a higher target following increased promotional efforts.
"The Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (MOTAC) and Tourism Kelantan are helping to promote the festival, including in Jakarta and southern Thailand.
"We are also expecting visitors from Singapore, Indonesia and other countries, while southern Thai visitors are also expected to make the trip across the border," he said.
He said admission to the festival was free, with the exhibition open from 9am to 10pm daily.
The festival is a joint effort involving the Kelantan State Museum Corporation, Kraftangan Malaysia and individual collectors.
Safaruddin said the event would provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the craftsmanship behind traditional weapons while learning about the state's royal history and cultural identity.
"These are not merely old weapons or artefacts. Each piece carries its own history and reflects the skills, traditions and identity of the people of Kelantan," he said.
Meanwhile, information displayed at the exhibition states that the crown was crafted during the reign of Sultan Ismail Ibni Almarhum Sultan Muhammad IV from 16 bungkal of pure gold and decorated with a young dala leaf motif.
The centre of the crown bears the emblem of the Kelantan state, while its pinnacle features a crescent moon and five-pointed star. Its interior is lined with royal blue velvet to accentuate the gleaming gold.
During the reign of Sultan Yahya Petra, 473 diamonds, 52 emeralds and rubies were added to the crown, while a further 721 diamonds and 44 emeralds were added during the reign of Sultan Ismail Petra.
With the royal crown taking centre stage, the festival offers visitors a rare glimpse into a part of Kelantan's royal heritage that has traditionally remained away from public view.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farmers bring bananas, cassava and coconuts to settle 3 billion rupiah fine
Article:
BENGKULU (Indonesia): Unable to pay a 3 billion rupiah (about RM688,000) fine, three farmers brought agricultural produce such as bananas, cassava and coconuts to court as payment after they were accused of cultivating land belonging to a palm oil company, reports said.
In a report published by Kompas.com, the three farmers were Harapandi, 50, Rasuli, 53, and Ibnu Amin, 44.
Harapandi said they were accused of cultivating the land and taking the company's oil palm fruit, but stressed that they had never seen the proceeds from the crops allegedly linked to the losses.
He said when they were asked to pay the fine, they could only bring agricultural produce they owned, namely cassava, bananas and coconuts, to the court.
"This is all we have. Please take our agricultural produce. There is no justice anymore," he said.
The court accepted the agricultural produce and recorded it in official documents as payment of the fine. Harapandi said they were summoned by the court after the company demanded payment of the fine imposed on them.
The dispute began in 2005 when about 50 farmers found that large areas of oil palm plantations had been abandoned.
Harapandi was quoted by Kompas.com as claiming that they first asked the company whether the land was covered by its cultivation rights (HGU).
"We asked before cultivating it, but at the time we were told that the area was not covered by the cultivation rights, so we cultivated it.
"However, the area was later claimed to be part of the cultivation rights. Our huts and crops were demolished, while we were evicted," he said.
The dispute continued until Aug 9, 2023, when the company filed a civil claim against the farmers, alleging that they had cultivated land covered by its HGU.
The Mukomuko District Court initially ordered the three farmers to pay a 1.3 billion rupiah (about RM297,000) fine before the case was taken to appeal and subsequently to Indonesia's Supreme Court.
At the final appeal stage, the fine was increased to 3 billion rupiah (about RM688,000), to be paid jointly by the three farmers.
Kompas.com said it had sought comments from the management and legal representatives of the palm oil company by telephone, but no response had been received when the report was published.
