Title: Malaysian Qualifications Agency says abolition of AUKU cannot be taken lightly, urges clear guidelines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) must be followed by the creation of an equivalent legal framework to guarantee the continuity of governance and quality of the country’s higher education at the global level.
Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Prof Datuk Dr Mohammad Shatar Sabran said any changes to the higher education legal framework must be made comprehensively and carefully to avoid gaps in terms of regulations, governance and institutional monitoring.
He said the higher education system needs clear guidelines and procedures to ensure that university management and administration remain orderly and accountable.
“Any decision regarding the abolition of AUKU must be preceded by a comprehensive approach as recommended by the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT), including a comprehensive assessment of the implications of changes to the higher education ecosystem.
“This approach is important to ensure that efforts to strengthen the country’s higher education system do not affect the government’s agenda to make Malaysia a global education hub,” he said in a statement today.
Mohammad Shatar said any proposal to abolish AUKU cannot be viewed lightly because the act is one of the important instruments that provides guidelines and a governance framework for the journey of higher education institutions (IPT).
Mohammad Shatar said the quality of national education today is highly regarded by the world and efforts to build the quality of national education that have been implemented since Merdeka need to be further strengthened.
In this regard, he called on the public to give full trust to KPT in its efforts to discuss matters related to the act.
He said it was also in line with the Malaysian Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035 which was launched in January through the agenda of the One Higher Education Act.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, while delivering the PKR Presidential Policy Address in conjunction with the PKR 2026 National Congress yesterday, announced that the government would abolish AUKU to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in the country.
Anwar said the decision was made following a memorandum and the views of the student leadership who wanted comprehensive changes to AUKU. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak skies turn grey, DOE warns haze plumes from Kalimantan push API into danger zone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 11am today, with the Serian district police headquarters (IPD) topping the list at 162.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said two other areas, Samarahan and Kuching, recorded API readings of 155 and 132, respectively, believed to be due to haze smoke moving in from various directions.
She said 65 other areas recorded moderate air quality levels.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah said according to the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report on August 15, 132 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 115 in Sumatra and six in Malaysia, comprising one each in Melaka and Johor and two each in Sarawak and Sabah.
“The Regional Haze Map released by ASMC today shows hotspots scattered across most of Kalimantan, with isolated hotspots also detected on Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, Sulawesi and southern Sumatra,” she said in a statement today.
Azuri Azizah said moderate smoke plumes were observed over southern and western Kalimantan, while light, localised smoke plumes were detected in southern and central Sumatra.
However, she said widespread cloud cover hampered observation of the current hotspot and haze situation.
She said the DOE had stepped up enforcement and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, in addition to regularly monitoring API readings.
“The National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate government agencies’ actions in dealing with open burning and the haze situation,” she said.
The public is urged to refrain from open burning and immediately report any such activities or fire incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution made PKR’s de facto number two as Nurul Izzah steps down
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution will take over the duties of PKR’s deputy president after incumbent Nurul Izzah Anwar announced she would “take leave”.
Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the handover at the party’s congress here this afternoon, where Nurul Izzah also gave a parting speech that called on the party to unite and galvanise its “differences” as a form of strength.
Anwar also gave full authority to PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to direct the party’s election campaigns, a move he suggested would streamline preparations and strategies to avoid confusion in the chain of command.
“He (Saifuddin) has been with me for decades and I know him very well,” Anwar said in a speech as he wound up this year’s congress.
”As for Amirudin he is given full trust… no more various ways. This time it’s one system, one strategy and a unified approach. Everyone must follow,” he added.
Two days ago Nurul Izzah cautioned the party about factionalism, saying that the party cannot remain strong if it is distracted by internal disputes.
Speaking at the joint Wanita Keadilan and Angkatan Muda Keadilan congress, she said the party risked weakening itself if factionalism continued to dominate.
Nurul Izzah, Anwar’s eldest daughter, said she will remain in the party but pursue a different path in her political struggle, expressing a preference for field work with civil society groups.
“You cannot please everyone; you can only remain true to yourself,” she said when opening the 2026 Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) and Wanita PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh on Friday.

Title: At DAP congress, most delegates back staying in Anwar govt, urge faster reforms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates debating whether the party should remain in the federal government today have largely backed staying until the end of the current term, while urging Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to accelerate reforms promised to Malaysians.
Speaking during the party’s national congress here, several delegates argued that leaving the unity government now would amount to abandoning voters and handing political advantage to rival parties.
Perak delegate and Sitiawan assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yeong said his position was simple: DAP should remain in the government until the end of the term.
“Previously, we fought and kept fighting until we won. Now that we have won, do we want to run away? No. We should stay once again,” he said.
Ng acknowledged DAP’s setbacks in the recent state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, but said the defeats should prompt the party to push harder for change rather than leave the government.
“We have to accept that this unity government has weaknesses. We need to accept that changes must be made, and we should urge our leaders and the PM to implement the reforms promised to the people, instead of leaving the government and disappointing the people even more,” he said.
He also questioned who would benefit if DAP walked away.
“If we leave, who benefits? Who will be happy? The answer may be MCA, PAS or Perikatan Nasional, which may take over the federal government after this,” he said.
Penang delegate Daniel Gooi Zi Sen, meanwhile, stressed the importance of political stability, pointing to the disruption caused by the Sheraton Move in 2020.
He said major projects had stalled during the period of political instability, while projects such as the LRT were now moving forward under the current administration.
“We cannot let political turmoil happen again,” he said, before asking delegates: “Did we fail as a federal government? Did we not do our job?”
Gooi’s argument was that the party should not disregard the progress made under the unity government despite its shortcomings.
Sarawak delegate Soo Tien Ren said he too would vote for DAP to remain in government, warning that leaving now would amount to “political suicide”.
“If we leave now, we will be committing political suicide. We will be abandoning Malaysians who believe in us, and abandoning our responsibility to correct our own mistakes,” he said.
However, Soo cautioned that merely remaining in Cabinet without clearly demonstrating what reforms DAP was pursuing could also prove politically damaging.
“If we stay, and all we can say is we remain in Cabinet and push for more reforms, but without telling Malaysians the reforms and the target, then staying turns into immediate political suicide and into slow political death.
“Between immediate suicide and slow death, I choose neither. I choose this party to survive and recover.”
Soo said DAP must acknowledge that it had not performed well enough and push Anwar for further reforms, including for the prime minister to relinquish the Finance portfolio and for the Budi95 subsidised petrol scheme to be restored to a 300-litre quota.
Kedah delegate Lim Hooi Yee similarly called on DAP to remain in the federal government until the end of the term.
“DAP must remain in the federal government until the end of the term. Leaving would mean betraying the King, the people and the principles of the party, which has fought for the people of Malaysia.
“The struggle is not over,” she said.
Lim said the results of the three state elections should instead serve as a warning for DAP to reflect on its performance.
“The results of the three state elections gave us different warnings. They are for us to reflect on, not to wash our hands of the matter and run away from responsibility,” she said.
DAP delegates are currently voting on whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the federal government.
The vote comes after party secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said he would leave the decision on DAP’s continued participation in the government to delegates.
The outcome is expected to be announced this afternoon.

Title: At DAP congress, Sangeet urges rethink of ties with Anwar, says PM has divided coalition, empowered Umno
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Wanita DAP legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo today called on the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) to reassess its relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of a vote at the national congress on whether DAP should remain in the federal government.
While favouring DAP’s continued participation in the federal government, Sangeet said the current coalition arrangement under Anwar had failed to unite its partners.
“Instead of bringing the coalition partners together, what has he done?
“He has divided us, pitted one against the other and empowered Umno.
“We cannot afford to ignore that,” she said in her debate speech on the motion to decide the party’s position in the federal unity government.
Sangeet said DAP’s decision to remain in the federal government should not be based merely on preserving political stability ahead of the next general election, but on using the remaining period to rebuild public trust, regain its voice and address issues on which it had previously remained silent.
“At the ministerial level, initiatives have been strong but we cannot ignore the larger problems that we are facing as a party.
“On too many issues, we have remained silent because we didn’t want to rock the boat,” she said.
She said the party could not ignore growing racial divisions and corruption-related scandals during its time in the federal government, warning that its silence on these issues had affected public confidence.
“We cannot run away from the fact that today, under our government, Malaysia is more divided on racial lines than ever before.
“We cannot deny that there are scandals relating to corruption that have escalated during the time that we have been in power,” she said.
She added that DAP came into power promising to eradicate corruption but questioned whether the party had done enough to address the issue.
“We have faced scandals involving our institutions, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), and our voters are asking: ‘Where is DAP? Where is your voice? Why are you silent?’”
She was referring to allegations of a so-called “corporate mafia” involving claims of collusion with the MACC to manipulate corporate takeovers through extortion and the exploitation of regulatory loopholes, including allegations implicating former MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki.
“I can assure you that when the scandal of the corporate mafia hit our news, our leaders in Cabinet stood there and asked themselves how they were going to defend this? It cannot be defended,” she added.
Sangeet also questioned whether DAP could genuinely work with its coalition partners, particularly Umno, which she said continued to openly attack the party despite being part of the federal government.
“But I do not say that it is because we are going to achieve the reforms we have promised all this while because if we were, we would have done it already.
“The fact is we cannot work with these coalition partners,” she said.
Sangeet said DAP should use the next 18 months in government to speak up on issues of concern and rebuild its credibility.
